questions.text: Where was William Shakespeare born?
questions.explanation: William Shakespeare was born inStratford-upon-Avon.

questions.text: Which TWO islands are closely linked to the UK but are not part of it?
questions.explanation: The Channel Islands and the Isle of Manare closely linked to the UK but are not part of it.

questions.text: Who gave Henry VIII the son he wanted, Edward?
questions.explanation: Jane Seymourgave Henry VIII the son he wanted, Edward.

questions.text: The Middle Ages or medieval times relate to the time that goes from the period after the Norman Conquest until the year:
questions.explanation: The period after the Norman Conquest up until about1485is called the Middle Ages (or the medieval period).

questions.text: Who is the heir to the throne of the UK?
questions.explanation: The King’s eldest son,Prince William (the Prince of Wales), is the heir to the throne.

questions.text: Which flower is associated with Wales?
questions.explanation: The daffodilis the flower associated with Wales.

questions.text: What was the nickname given to the Scottish poet Robert Burns?
questions.explanation: Robert Burns, a Scottish poet, was Known in Scotland as‘The Bard’.

questions.text: When was Ireland divided into two countries?
questions.explanation: In 1921 a peace treaty was signed and in1922Ireland became two countries.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a city of the UK?
questions.explanation: Dublinis not a city of the UK.

questions.text: When is Bonfire Night celebrated?
questions.explanation: Bonfire Night is celebrated on the5th of November.

questions.text: What is the name of the event that refers to the 6 June 1944 when Allied Forces landed in Normandy aiming to attack Hitler’s forces in Western Europe during World War II?
questions.explanation: ‘D-Day’refers to the 6th of June 1944, when allied forces landed in Normandy aiming to attack Hitler’s forces in Western Europe during World War II.

questions.text: In the UK, many people continue to visit the countryside for holidays and for leisure activities such as  walking, camping and fishing:
questions.explanation: Many people continue to visit the countryside for holidays and for leisure activities such as  walking, camping and fishing.

questions.text: What is the name of the building where the Northern Ireland Assembly meet?
questions.explanation: In Northern Ireland elected members, known as MLAs, meet in the Northern Ireland Assembly atStormont, in Belfast.

questions.text: Which British Prime Minister led the Conservative government from 1979 to 1990?
questions.explanation: Margaret Thatcher, Britain’s first woman Prime Minister, led the Conservative government from 1979 to 1990.

questions.text: Which of the following civilisations is known for having built roads and public buildings, creating a structure of law and having introduced new plants and animals in Britain?
questions.explanation: The Romansremained in Britain for 400 years. They built roads and public buildings, created a structure of law, and introduced new plants and animals.

questions.text: How often does the Edinburgh Festival take place?
questions.explanation: The Edinburgh Festival takes place in Edinburgh, Scotland,every summer.

questions.text: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Commonwealth?
questions.explanation: Zimbabweis not a member of the Commonwealth.

questions.text: What marked the beginning of what is called ‘constitutional monarchy’?
questions.explanation: The laws passed after the Glorious Revolutionare the beginning of what is called ‘constitutional monarchy’.

options.text: The laws passed after the Glorious Revolution
A speech given by the King
The emergence of new ideas about politics, philosophy and science
The development of the Bessemer process

questions.text: What name is given to the day that marks the end of the Ramadan, when Muslims have fasted for a month?
questions.explanation: Eid a-Fitrcelebrates the end of Ramadan, when Muslims have fasted for a month.

questions.text: Who is the fastest person to have sailed around the world single-handed?
questions.explanation: Dame Ellen MacArthuris a yachtswoman and in 2004 became the fastest person to sail around the world single-handed.

questions.text: Who makes the decisions on government policies in the UK?
questions.explanation: Decisions on government policies are made bythe Prime Minister and cabinet.

options.text: Only the Prime Minister can make the decisions on government policies
The Prime Minister and the Cabinet
The monarch and the Prime Minister

questions.text: Where does the most famous sailing event in the UK take place?
questions.explanation: The most famous sailing event in the UK takes place atCowes on the Isle of Wight.

questions.text: How often is the electoral register updated?
questions.explanation: The electoral register is updatedevery year in September or October.

questions.text: What do you need to drive a car in the UK?
questions.explanation: To drive a car in the UK you need a driving licence, a valid motor insurance, a MOT certificate (for cars over three years old) and the road tax.

options.text: A driving licence, a valid motor insurance, a MOT certificate and the road tax
A driving licence and a valid motor insurance only
A driving licence and a MOT certificate only
